# apex-commons

The shared core behind the ApexCharts product family: licensing, watermarking, theming, internationalisation, spring motion and coordinated filtering.

It exists because these things are not chart-specific. A licence key, a theme token, a text direction and a filter mean the same thing to a chart, a tree, a sankey diagram and a grid, and each of those having its own copy meant four implementations drifting apart. Anything the family needs to agree on lives here, so it is agreed on once.

Most users never install this directly. It arrives as a dependency of the product you are using, and the parts you touch are reached through that product's own API. Install it yourself when you are building against several of them at once, or using the crossfilter engine with no chart present.

## Installation

```bash
npm install apex-commons
```

## Licensing

`LicenseManager` is the enforcement path for the whole family, so a key set once here is honoured by every Apex product on the page.

```js
import {LicenseManager} from 'apex-commons';

LicenseManager.setLicense('your-license-key');
```

Without a valid key a product keeps working and carries a trial watermark. That is deterrence and honest-customer compliance rather than DRM: no feature is ever degraded.

The key is shared by every product on the page, so a later `setLicense` never takes away what an earlier one established: a different key is ignored, with a warning, when it is invalid or when its plan is lower than the valid key already in force (a Pro key after a Premium one). Call `setLicense('')` first to move to a lower plan on purpose.

The products this serves are free under the Community terms for organisations under the revenue threshold, and need a Commercial licence otherwise. See <https://apexcharts.com/pricing>.

| Member                    | Description                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `LicenseManager`          | Static class holding the licence for every Apex product on the page.     |
| `setLicense`              | Set the key. Call before creating any instance. See above.               |
| `getKey`                  | The key currently in force, or `null`.                                   |
| `isLicenseValid`          | Whether the key in force is valid right now.                             |
| `isKeyValid`              | Whether a given key would be valid, without setting it.                  |
| `getLicenseStatus`        | The full `LicenseValidationResult` for the key in force.                 |
| `validateKey`             | Validate a given key and return its result, without setting it.          |
| `onChange`                | Subscribe to licence changes. Returns an unsubscribe function.           |
| `LicenseData`             | The decoded payload: plan, issue and expiry dates, optional domains.     |
| `LicenseValidationResult` | The outcome of a check: whether it is valid, and why not when it is not. |
| `LicenseChangeListener`   | The callback shape `onChange` takes.                                     |

### Plan tiers

Whether a licence covers a feature, in one place, so every Apex product answers it the same way.

`planAtLeast` has one hard boundary and one deliberate softness. Without a valid licence it always returns `false`. With a valid licence whose plan string is not recognised it returns `true` and warns once, because the holder has a signed, unexpired key: refusing them a feature over a string we failed to map is worse than granting one. Gating here is deterrence and honest-customer compliance, not DRM.

```js
import {planAtLeast} from 'apex-commons';

if (planAtLeast('premium')) {
  // show the tool
}
```

| Member          | Description                                                                            |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `planAtLeast`   | Whether the licence in force covers a feature needing at least the given plan.         |
| `currentPlan`   | The plan the licence grants, or `null`. For display; use `planAtLeast` to gate.        |
| `normalisePlan` | Resolve a raw plan string to a known plan, ignoring case and space. `null` if unknown. |
| `PLAN_ORDER`    | Every plan string a key may carry, in commercial ladder order. Not the gating order.   |
| `PLAN_ALIASES`  | Plan strings that may appear in issued keys but are not current plan names.            |
| `ApexPlan`      | The plan names: `community`, `pro`, `premium`, `embedded`, `oem`.                      |

**There are three gating levels, not five.** `community` < `pro` < `premium`, and `embedded` and `oem` rank **equal to** `premium` rather than above it. That is because they are not a higher feature tier: they are a second axis. `pro` and `premium` price the features a product uses, while `embedded` and `oem` price redistributing it, and an OEM licence is sold with every licensed feature included. So a key carrying `oem` grants exactly what `premium` grants, no more, and `premium` is the ceiling. A feature gating above it would be reachable by no purchasable licence at all.

The two axes are bought together, not instead of each other: an OEM customer buys redistribution rights per application **and** a developer licence for each developer who works on that application. Neither axis is visible here, because seats and application counts are a billing concern and this module only reads what a key already carries.

Both strings stay in the vocabulary rather than being removed, because `planAtLeast` fails open on a plan it does not recognise: drop them and a key carrying one would be granted everything, which is the opposite of the intent.

`community` never appears in a key, because that tier is issued none, so `planAtLeast('community')` means "holds any licence at all".

`oem` was called `enterprise` until 2026-09-14, and `PLAN_ALIASES` maps the old string so a key carrying it still resolves to a real rank rather than fail-opening.

### Watermark

The trial mark an unlicensed product adds to its container.

| Member             | Description                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Watermark`        | Static class that adds, finds and removes the trial mark.    |
| `WatermarkOptions` | Options accepted by `add` and `remove`.                      |
| `ATTR`             | The attribute the mark carries, for finding it.              |
| `add`              | Add the mark to a container. Returns the element, or `null`. |
| `remove`           | Remove the mark from a container.                            |
| `exists`           | Whether a container currently carries a mark.                |
| `node`             | The container's own mark (a direct child), or `null`.        |
| `applyStyles`      | Apply the mark's styles to an element.                       |
| `untrack`          | Stop tracking a container, without removing its mark.        |

`add` and `remove` track the container, and a later licence change (a late `setLicense`, or a signature failing verification) adds or removes its mark again. A product calls `untrack` when it is destroyed and leaves its container to the page. Each container answers for its own mark only, so `remove` on a container never erases the mark of another product's container nested inside it. With `requires` set, a valid key whose plan is too low logs a warning once per page saying why the mark stays. `WatermarkOptions` steers that:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `manage` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether this package reconciles the container against the page licence. Pass `false` when the product decides for itself. |
| `requires` | `ApexPlan` | `undefined` | The lowest plan that removes the mark from this container, held per container and honoured on every reconcile. Without it any valid licence removes it. Decide `add` or `remove` at render with `planAtLeast(requires)` so the two agree. |

```js
import {planAtLeast, Watermark} from 'apex-commons';

// A product sold from Premium up: a valid Pro key keeps the mark.
const options = {requires: 'premium'};
if (planAtLeast('premium')) Watermark.remove(container, options);
else Watermark.add(container, options);
```

## Internationalisation

Every product owns its message dictionary, its locale packs and where its text goes. What lives here is the plumbing they share: merging a locale pack and a caller's overrides onto the English defaults, rendering a message, formatting numbers in a locale, reading what a person typed through an input method, and marking an element's direction and language.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TextDirection` | `'ltr'`, `'rtl'` or `'auto'`. |
| `applyDirection` | Set text direction on an element, resolving `'auto'` against the document. |
| `isRTL` | Whether a direction resolves to right-to-left, given an optional element. |
| `applyLang` | Set or remove the BCP 47 `lang` attribute (and `xml:lang` on SVG) on an element. |
| `resolveMessages` | Merge override layers (for example a locale pack, then user overrides) onto a product's defaults, safely for JSON input. |
| `formatMessage` | Render a template (`{name}`, `{n, number}`, `{n, plural, ...}`) or a message function to plain text. |
| `MessageTemplate` | A template string or a function of the params. |
| `MessageParams` | Values for `{name}` placeholders. |
| `MessageOverrides` | Sparse overrides for a dictionary, where function entries also take template strings. |
| `ResolvedMessages` | A dictionary after merging, where function entries may hold templates. |
| `formatNumber` | Format a number with a cached `Intl.NumberFormat` (compact 万/億, currency, percent). |
| `FormatNumberOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` plus `locale`. |
| `formatNumberRange` | Format a numeric range with the locale's separator (`10～20`), safe for equal or non-finite ends. |
| `FormatNumberRangeOptions` | Range options: `separator` and a per-end `format` callback. |
| `parseNumberInput` | Read typed text as a number, folding full-width digits and IME punctuation. |
| `parseLocaleNumberInput` | `parseNumberInput` with the locale's grouping read first. |
| `normalizeInput` | Fold text for search matching: NFKC, plus optional kana and case folds. |
| `NormalizeInputOptions` | `kana` and `lowerCase` folds. |
| `trackCompositions` | Install the document-wide composition tracking behind `isComposing`. |
| `isComposing` | Whether an event belongs to an open IME composition. |
| `LocalePack` | Shared contract for first-party locale packs. |
| `LocalePackStatus` | `'draft'` or `'reviewed'`. |

```js
import {formatMessage, formatNumber, resolveMessages} from 'apex-commons';

const messages = resolveMessages(defaults, pack.messages, userMessages);

formatMessage('{count} selected', {count: 3}); // '3 selected'
formatMessage('{n, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}}', {n: 1200}, 'en'); // '1,200 tasks'
formatNumber(123456789, {locale: 'ja', notation: 'compact'}); // '1.2億'
```

Templates are plain strings, so a dictionary survives JSON and a .NET `Dictionary<string,string>` unchanged. A placeholder with no value, and any `{...}` text that is not a placeholder, prints as written. `formatMessage` returns plain text: escaping it for HTML is the caller's job.

### Importing only the i18n helpers

From 0.11.0 the same helpers are also published on their own at the `apex-commons/i18n` subpath, as ESM and CommonJS with type declarations:

```js
import {isComposing, trackCompositions} from 'apex-commons/i18n';
```

The subpath carries none of the licensing, watermark, theming or motion code, and every helper in it is free of import-time side effects, so a bundle pays only for what it imports: `isComposing` with `trackCompositions` adds well under half a kilobyte gzipped. Nothing in it touches `window` or `document` when it is imported, so it is safe to import during server-side rendering.

## Shadow DOM

Helpers that give the same answer whether a product renders in the light DOM, in a shadow root, or in a shadow root nested inside another. Each takes the product's own element and works out its root from it.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `rootOf` | The root an element renders in: its `ShadowRoot`, or its `Document`. |
| `eventOrigin` | The node an event really started on, through shadow retargeting. Use it for "was this click inside?" tests in `document` listeners. |
| `activeElementIn` | The focused element, followed down through open shadow roots. |
| `queryInRoot` | `querySelector` in the element's root first, then in the document. |
| `queryAllInRoot` | `querySelectorAll` in the element's root, or in the document when the root has no match. |
| `injectStyle` | Add a stylesheet to the element's root once, prepended so page rules win, or right after another sheet with `after`. Returns a release function; the sheet goes with its last user. |
| `InjectStyleOptions` | Options for `injectStyle`: a CSP `nonce`, and `after`, the id of a sheet in the same root this one must follow (an override sheet after the product's main one, in either arrival order). |
| `styleSheetsFor` | Every stylesheet that applies to an element, including each enclosing root's own and adopted sheets. For exporters. |

## Theming

A page declares the `--apx-*` custom properties once on `:root` and every Apex product on it follows. Each product resolves its options in one order, highest first: an option the page passed, the product's own CSS variable, the `--apx-*` tokens, a named theme or explicit palette, the page's design system (Ignite UI, `--ig-*`, when its add-on is loaded), then the built-in default. "Passed" means the page handed the option over, tracked by the product, never "differs from the default", so a product already themed through its own options is untouched.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ApxTokens` | The resolved token set: accent, foreground, grid, surface, font, radius factor, the series palette, and the raised and overlay roles the merged view can carry. |
| `APX_TOKEN_VARS` | The custom property name for each token role. |
| `APX_SERIES_VAR_PREFIX` | Prefix for the ordered series palette, `--apx-series-N`. |
| `readTokens` | Read the `--apx-*` tokens currently in force on an element. Values are the cascade's text, never normalised. |
| `resolveTokenLayers` | Read the `--apx-*` tokens, a named theme's tokens and the design system at an element, each layer apart, from one computed style. |
| `TokenLayers` | What `resolveTokenLayers` returns: `css`, `named` and `designSystem`. |
| `TokenLayerOptions` | `css: false` skips the `--apx-*` read, `designSystem: false` the design system (read by default), `host` reads through a `ThemeHost`. |
| `resolveTokenLayer` | The same layers folded into one `ApxTokens`, CSS over the named theme over the design system. The design system is read only with `designSystem: true`. |
| `MergedTokenLayerOptions` | Options for `resolveTokenLayer`: the opt-in `designSystem`, the product's `mode` for the variant gate, and `builtinSeries` to complete the design system's series rows. |
| `layerValue` | One role through the three layers, for a product that writes the winner back into its own state. |
| `pickToken` | Resolve one value through the precedence order above. The option ranks first only with `explicit: true`; below every layer the option is kept, and only a missing one takes the fallback. |
| `TokenPrecedenceInput` | The candidates `pickToken` chooses between. |
| `ApxTheme` | A named theme: the token roles it contributes. |
| `registerTheme` | Register or override a named theme on the shared registry. |
| `getTheme` | Look up a registered theme by name. |
| `registeredThemes` | The names currently registered. |
| `unregisterTheme` | Remove a registered theme. |
| `OwnedToken` | Tracks a custom property a product set itself, so it can put back what it found. |
| `resolveOwnedRole` | Resolve every place one role writes to, keeping the page's own values and replacing only what the product wrote. |
| `OwnedSlot` | One place a role writes to: what it holds now, whether the page passed that value, and its own defaults and fallback. |
| `OwnedRoleInput` | Input to `resolveOwnedRole`: the slots, the winning layer value, the value written last render and the values that count as unset. |
| `OwnedRoleResult` | What each slot should hold, which of them changed, and the snapshot to pass back next render. |
| `OSThemeWatcher` | Watches the operating system's light and dark preference. Its `supports` getter says which queries the environment can evaluate. |
| `OSThemeState` | The current OS preference. |
| `OSThemeWatcherOptions` | Options for the watcher, including the `host` to read media queries through. |
| `OSThemeSupport` | Which of the two preference queries the environment can evaluate. |
| `ThemeHost` | Where the theme readers get computed styles and media queries from, for a server or test that has no page. |
| `DEFAULT_THEME_HOST` | The page's own `getComputedStyle` and `matchMedia`, each guarded. |
| `CSSLike` | The part of a computed style declaration the readers use. |

### Design system (Ignite UI)

Ignite UI theming is an add-on. Load it once and ApexTree, ApexSankey and ApexGantt follow the Ignite UI theme on the page: palette, text, gridlines, surfaces, font, light or dark. Without it the `--ig-*` tokens are ignored, with no error and no custom-property read; the `--apx-*` tokens work either way.

```js
import 'apex-commons/ignite-ui';
```

Or load `apex-commons.ignite-ui.min.js` with a script tag, or `require('apex-commons/ignite-ui')`. Products that bundle commons re-export it as their own entry (`apextree/ignite-ui` and so on), so a page normally loads its product's entry rather than this one. Import it before the first render; a product rendered earlier picks it up on its next render. A product's `designSystem: false` (or `tokens: false`) still turns it off. With several of these products on one page, load the add-on from the newest package: the newest copy is the one they all read. Each copy ranks by the commons version it was built from, and a pre-release ranks below its release.

ApexCharts is the exception: it reads only its own add-on, `apexcharts/features/ignite-ui`, which pairs the map with the chart stylesheet's Ignite UI rules. Neither this entry nor a Tree, Sankey or Gantt add-on themes a chart, and a newer copy from another product never replaces the one ApexCharts reads. Its add-on registers the map for the other products too, but from a script tag only once `apexcharts.js` has loaded.

Series 1 to 6 are the primary, secondary, info, success, warn and error colours (their seed, else 500), series 7 to 12 the same six at 300 and 13 to 18 at 700. Text, muted text and hairlines are gray 800, 600 and 300. The paper is never painted. Text and hairline colours apply only when the product's mode matches the sheet's `--ig-theme-variant`, and a dark variant turns a product with no mode of its own dark.

The main entry carries the lookup and the types only:

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `readDesignSystemLayer` | Read the design system visible at an element through the loaded add-ons. Null when none is loaded (before any custom-property read) or the design system is not on the page. Every colour is resolved and clipped to sRGB; a token that does not resolve counts as absent. |
| `DesignSystemLayer` | What one read found: the series rows, the colour roles, the font, the variant and the paper for raster exports. `color(role, mode)` applies the variant gate; `palette(builtin)` fills the series rows' gaps from the product's built-in palette and is never null (with no row resolved it is the built-in palette). |
| `ReadDesignSystemOptions` | `host` or a computed style `cs` the caller already has, and `adapter` to read that one adapter instead of every loaded one. |
| `designSystemColor` | `layer.color(role, mode)`, or undefined without a layer. |
| `DesignSystemColorRole` | The colour roles a design system can fill. |
| `DesignSystemTokenMap` | A mapping from roles to chains of custom-property names, read left to right. |
| `DesignSystemAdapter` | What an add-on registers: a name, a revision and a `read` function. Internal: there is no API to add a design system. |
| `fillVariantMode` | Fill an unset mode from the sheet's variant. Returns a record when it filled dark. |
| `takeBackVariantMode` | Take a variant-filled dark mode back on a later render, so the light defaults run again. |
| `VariantModeRecord` | Present when the product's dark mode came from the variant. |
| `VariantModeInput` | The product's mode, and whether the OS owns it. |
| `VariantTakeBack` | What `takeBackVariantMode` decided, with the state to restore. |
| `modePaper` | The on-screen paper: a dark mode the variant filled stays transparent unless the page set a background. |
| `rasterPaper` | The opaque base of a raster export. |
| `ModePaperInput` | Input to `modePaper` and `rasterPaper`. |

`apex-commons/ignite-ui` exports:

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `IGNITE_UI_ADAPTER` | The adapter the import registered. A product that pairs the map with its own stylesheet passes it to `readDesignSystemLayer` as `adapter`, so a newer copy another product registered cannot drive half of it. |
| `IGNITE_UI_TOKENS` | The Ignite UI mapping as frozen data, the same object the adapter and the generated CSS use. |

### Generated CSS

A product that themes in CSS only takes the Ignite UI mapping as `var()` chains, generated from `IGNITE_UI_TOKENS` when commons builds. Each chain reads the product's own variable, then `--apx-*`, then `--ig-*`, then the product's default. These files need no add-on: a page opts in by loading them.

| File or member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `apex-commons/css/igniteui.css` | One chain per role on `:host` (`--_apx-grid`, `--_apx-series-1`, ...), plus `:host([design-system='off'])` and `:host([tokens='off'])` rules. A web component adopts it and reads a role with its own default: `var(--my-border, var(--_apx-grid, #e5e7eb))`. |
| `apex-commons/css/_igniteui.scss` | The roles as a Sass map, with a `chain()` function and a `declarations` mixin that take the product's own names and defaults. |
| `designSystemCss` | From `apex-commons/ignite-ui/css`: the same chains for a build script, a selector, the product's declarations and the optional off rules in, CSS text out. Build time only: ES only, and it registers nothing. |
| `DesignSystemCssOptions` | Input to `designSystemCss`: `selector`, `declarations`, and the optional `designSystemOff` and `tokensOff` selectors. |
| `DesignSystemCssDeclaration` | One declaration: the custom property the product's rules read, the role it takes, the product's own variables and its default. |
| `DesignSystemCssRole` | The roles a declaration can take. |

The chains differ from the JS reader in three ways. Token values are used as the sheet wrote them, not clipped to sRGB. There is no variant gate, so a product whose mode can differ from the sheet's writes that mode's rules without the design system. And series rows fall through one by one: the JS products read `--apx-series-N` up to its first gap and let a non-empty list replace the design system's rows, while each CSS row falls to its own `--ig-*` chain, so a page that sets only some `--apx-series-N` can see different series colours in the two.

## Colour

One colour reader for the family, so every product reads a CSS colour the same way. Parsing is local where it can be and falls back to a canvas for the rest (named colours, `oklch()`, `lab()`, `color-mix()`); under SSR the canvas readers return null.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Rgba` | `[r, g, b, a]`: sRGB channels 0 to 255, then the alpha 0 to 1. |
| `toColor` | Any element-independent CSS colour as `#rrggbb`, or `rgba()` when translucent, clipped to sRGB. Null when it cannot be read. |
| `toRgba` | The same colour as `Rgba`. Canvas answers are cached. |
| `parseColor` | Any CSS colour as `Rgba`; one that depends on an element (`var()`, `currentColor`) is resolved inside the element you pass. |
| `resolveColor` | The computed colour of a value inside an element, as the browser's text. |
| `paintRgba` | Read a colour by painting it on a canvas. |
| `isColor` | Whether the browser accepts a value as a CSS colour. |
| `elementDependent` | Whether a value's colour depends on an element or the OS theme. |
| `parseLocal` | Parse a colour without a browser: hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `color(srgb ...)` and `transparent`, in the strict CSS grammar, clipped to sRGB. |
| `parseHexRgb` | The charts' fast, lax hex and `rgb()` parser. |
| `parseColorSrgb` | Parse `color(srgb ...)`, the form browsers compute `color-mix()` and relative colours to. |
| `parseHsl` | Parse `hsl()` and `hsla()`. |
| `parseOklab` | Parse `oklab()` and `oklch()`, clipped to sRGB. |
| `formatColor` | An `Rgba` as `#rrggbb`, or `rgba()` when translucent. |
| `luminance` | WCAG relative luminance, 0 to 1. |
| `contrastRatio` | WCAG contrast ratio between two colours, 1 to 21. |
| `luma` | BT.601 luma, 0 to 1. |
| `isDark` | Whether a colour reads as dark. A missing or transparent colour reads as light. |
| `readableOn` | Whichever of two text colours has the higher contrast on a background. |
| `shadeRgb` | Blend toward white or black, channel by channel. |
| `shadeOklab` | Move OkLab lightness, keeping hue and chroma. |
| `adjustHsl` | Rotate hue and move saturation and lightness. |
| `mixCss` | Blend toward white or black as a CSS `color-mix()`, for a colour only the browser can read. |
| `OkLab` | `[L, a, b]`: perceptual lightness, then the two opponent axes. |
| `rgbToOklab` | OkLab of sRGB channels. |
| `oklabToRgb` | sRGB channels of an OkLab colour, clipped to the sRGB range. |

## Motion

A headless spring driver, shared so that motion feels the same across the family. It computes values and holds no opinion about what draws them.

| Member                        | Description                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Spring`                      | One spring: its current value, velocity, target and rest thresholds.          |
| `makeSpring`                  | Create a spring at a value, with a stiffness and damping.                     |
| `stepSpring`                  | Advance a spring by a timestep. Returns whether it is still moving.           |
| `retarget`                    | Point a spring at a new target, keeping its velocity.                         |
| `snapSpring`                  | Move a spring to a value immediately, clearing velocity.                      |
| `SpringRest`                  | The velocity and displacement below which a spring counts as arrived.         |
| `UNIT_REST`                   | Rest thresholds for springs running over a 0 to 1 range, rather than pixels.  |
| `SpringPreset`                | `'crisp'`, `'gentle'` or `'snappy'`.                                          |
| `SPRING_PRESETS`              | The stiffness and damping pair behind each preset.                            |
| `resolveSpring`               | The pair for a preset, falling back to the default.                           |
| `CAMERA_SPRING`               | The pair used for pan and zoom, which wants less overshoot than content.      |
| `WAVE_STAGGER_MS`             | Delay between neighbours in a staggered entrance.                             |
| `SpringScene`                 | Drives many named springs on one animation loop, with a single rest callback. |
| `SpringSceneOptions`          | Options for a scene, including its clock.                                     |
| `SpringValues`                | The current value of every spring in a scene, by name.                        |
| `SceneObjectOptions`          | Options for one object added to a scene.                                      |
| `SceneClock`                  | The scene's time source. Substitutable, so tests need no timers.              |
| `diffNodes`                   | Split previous and next id sets into entering, surviving and leaving.         |
| `NodeDiff`                    | The result of `diffNodes`.                                                    |
| `ringDistances`               | Distance of each node from a set of roots, for staggering a wave outwards.    |
| `ReducedMotionWatcher`        | Watches the user's reduced-motion preference.                                 |
| `ReducedMotionWatcherOptions` | Options for the watcher.                                                      |

## Crossfilter

Coordinated filtering across any number of views. One shared record set, and per view a dimension (`row => key`), a reduction and a filter.

A view's aggregation is computed over the records passing every **other** view's filter, never its own, so each view keeps showing what else is reachable instead of collapsing to its own selection. A view's own filter only marks which of its buckets are selected.

Because a dimension is an arbitrary function, a map region, a tree subtree, a sankey link, a grid column and a chart category are all the same thing to it, and a set of views can coordinate with no chart present at all.

```js
import {Crossfilter} from 'apex-commons';

const cf = Crossfilter.getOrCreate({id: 'audit'});
cf.setRecords(rows);
cf.registerDimension('byRegion', {dimension: (r) => r.region});
cf.on('change', () => render(cf.aggregateAll()));
cf.filter('byRegion', ['EU']);
```

| Member              | Description                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Crossfilter`       | The coordinator.                                                   |
| `getOrCreate`       | Static. The coordinator for an id, creating it if needed.          |
| `get`               | Static. The coordinator for an id, or `null`.                      |
| `setRecords`        | Replace the shared record set.                                     |
| `registerDimension` | Add or replace a view's dimension and reduction.                   |
| `hasDimension`      | Whether a view is registered.                                      |
| `removeDimension`   | Remove a view.                                                     |
| `filter`            | Set a view's filter.                                               |
| `toggleKey`         | Add or remove one key from a view's filter.                        |
| `filterOf`          | A view's current filter, or `null`.                                |
| `clear`             | Clear one view's filter.                                           |
| `reset`             | Clear every filter.                                                |
| `aggregateFor`      | The aggregation for one view.                                      |
| `aggregateAll`      | The aggregation for every registered view.                         |
| `filteredRecords`   | Records passing every filter, optionally excluding one view's own. |
| `filteredRows`      | Records passing every filter.                                      |
| `state`             | A snapshot of records, filters and aggregations.                   |
| `on`                | Subscribe to an event. Returns an unsubscribe function.            |
| `off`               | Remove a handler.                                                  |
| `dataTable`         | Render a paged table of the filtered rows into an element.         |

### Crossfilter types

| Type                  | Description                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CrossfilterOptions`  | Options for `getOrCreate`, including the shared `id`.         |
| `CrossfilterRow`      | One record. Shape is entirely the caller's business.          |
| `CrossfilterState`    | The snapshot `state()` returns.                               |
| `CrossfilterEvent`    | The events a coordinator emits.                               |
| `CrossfilterListener` | The callback shape `on` takes.                                |
| `DimensionSpec`       | A view's dimension, reduction, ordering and binning.          |
| `DimensionAccessor`   | Maps a row to this view's key.                                |
| `DimensionType`       | Whether a dimension is categorical or numeric.                |
| `DimensionOrder`      | How a view's buckets are ordered.                             |
| `BinSpec`             | How a numeric dimension is bucketed.                          |
| `ReduceSpec`          | How rows in a bucket become a scalar.                         |
| `Reducer`             | A custom reduction function.                                  |
| `FilterInput`         | What `filter` accepts: a set of keys, or a numeric range.     |
| `Aggregate`           | Union of the aggregation shapes. Narrow it before reading.    |
| `CategoryAggregate`   | A flat list of keys and values.                               |
| `RangeAggregate`      | A numeric range aggregation.                                  |
| `MatrixAggregate`     | A two-dimensional aggregation, which has no flat `keys` list. |
| `DataTableOptions`    | Options for `dataTable`.                                      |
| `DataTableColumn`     | One column in a data table.                                   |
| `DataTableHandle`     | The handle `dataTable` returns.                               |

## Indicators

Moving-window indicators as pure functions, lifted out of apexstock so the chart family and the stock product share one implementation. Each takes `Array<number | null>` and returns the same length, with `null` wherever a value is not defined.

A window containing a gap yields `null` rather than an average of however many values were present, which would quietly compute a mean of four and show it beside means of ten.

`sma` is slice-invariant: a window averages to the same value whatever precedes it, so `sma(values.slice(i - period + 1, i + 1), period)` at its last position equals `sma(values, period)[i]` exactly. That is what lets a streaming consumer extend a series by recomputing only the tail window. It costs a running total, so `sma` is O(n \* period).

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sma` | Trailing simple moving average, aligned to the last position in each window. Slice-invariant, as above. |
| `ema` | Exponential moving average, seeded from the first complete simple window rather than the first value. A gap ends the run and the next complete window starts a new one. |
| `bollinger` | A simple moving average with a moving standard deviation either side, using the population denominator, which is the convention for this band. |
| `Bands` | What `bollinger` returns: `middle`, `upper` and `lower`, each the length of the input. |

```js
import {bollinger, ema, sma} from 'apex-commons';

sma([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 3); // [null, null, 2, 3, 4, 5]
ema([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 3); // [null, null, 2, 3, 4]
bollinger([2, 4, 4], 3, 2).upper;
```

## Histogram binning

Observations in, bin edges and counts out. Pure arithmetic, so it is testable on its own and inert under SSR.

Gaps mean the opposite of what they mean above. A moving average over a window containing a gap is undefined, because the window is a claim about a stretch of the series. A histogram is a tally of the observations that exist, so a gap is simply not one; `histogram` skips them and reports how many it skipped.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `histogram` | Bin a series and count it in one call, tolerating gaps. The convenience most callers want. |
| `computeBinning` | Choose bin edges for a set of finite observations. Precedence: an explicit `binWidth`, then an explicit bin count, then a named rule. |
| `binCounts` | Count observations into a set of edges. |
| `binIndexOf` | The bin holding one value, or `-1` outside the edges. Bins are half-open except the last, which includes its upper edge. |
| `quantileSorted` | Quantile of an ascending-sorted array, by the "type 7" definition that R, NumPy and a spreadsheet's QUARTILE all share. |
| `Histogram` | What `histogram` returns: a `Binning` plus `counts`, `midpoints`, `total` and `missing`. |
| `Binning` | `edges`, `binWidth`, the `rule` that actually chose the width, and whether the count was `capped`. |
| `BinOptions` | `bins` (a rule name or a fixed count), `binWidth`, and a `range` to frame the bins on so several histograms share a scale. |
| `BinRule` | The named rules: `auto`, `fd`, `rice`, `scott`, `sqrt`, `sturges`. `auto` is the narrower of `fd` and `sturges`, falling back to `sturges` when the IQR is zero. |

```js
import {histogram} from 'apex-commons';

const h = histogram([1, 2, 2, 3, null, 9]);
h.counts; // observations per bin
h.missing; // 1
```

## Browser support

Every module is SSR-safe: nothing touches `document` at import time, and the pieces that need the DOM take the element they act on. `Crossfilter` is DOM-free apart from its optional `dataTable` helper.
